name: RoboBench
description: A comprehensive evaluation benchmark for multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as embodied brains in robotic manipulation. RoboBench systematically evaluates MLLMs across five dimensions—instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis—spanning 14 capabilities, 25 tasks, and 6092 QA pairs.

creator.name: Yulin Luo, Chun-Kai Fan, Menghang Dong, Jiayu Shi, Mengdi Zhao, Bo-Wen Zhang, Cheng Chi, Jiaming Liu, Gaole Dai, Rongyu Zhang, Ruichuan An, Kun Wu, Zhengping Che, Shaoxuan Xie, Guocai Yao, Zhongxia Zhao, Pengwei Wang, Guang Liu, Zhongyuan Wang, Tiejun Huang, Shanghang Zhang

citeAs: Yulin Luo et al. RoboBench: A Comprehensive Evaluation Benchmark for Multimodal Large Language Models as Embodied Brain. arXiv:2510.17801v1 [cs.RO] 20 Oct 2025
rai:dataCollection: RoboBench combines data from large-scale real-world robotic datasets and in-house collection. The benchmark constructs datasets from open-source robotic data (Open X-Embodiment, RH20T, RDT-1B, RoboMIND, LIBERO, and others) enriched with MLLM-provided annotations and human expert annotations. Data collection follows dimension-specific workflows: instruction data uses paired explicit-implicit design from daily-life scenarios; perception data combines curated static attributes with GPT-generated functional properties; planning data is extracted from high-quality robotic videos with Gemini-generated structured annotations refined by human annotators; affordance data samples representative frames with three types of annotations (static, dynamic, mobile); failure analysis data includes execution-level failures from RoboMIND labeled by experts and synthesized planning-level failures.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator, Web API
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Data sources include: Open X-Embodiment Collaboration robotic datasets, RH20T (Fang et al. 2023), RDT-1B (Liu et al. 2024b), RoboMIND (Wu et al. 2024), LIBERO (Liu et al. 2023a), and other large-scale real robotic manipulation datasets (Lin et al. 2024a, Liu et al. 2024c, Mu et al. 2023, Yang et al. 2024, Bu et al. 2025). Additional in-house data collection was performed to ensure diversity across embodiments, objects, viewpoints, and task settings.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Data manipulation includes: (1) Explicit-to-implicit instruction conversion using LLMs to rewrite explicit instructions into demand-based requests; (2) Video frame extraction and sampling for planning tasks; (3) Synthesis of planning-level failures by perturbing correct instructions (wrong object, missing step, wrong order); (4) Object property generation using GPT for functional attributes with distractor creation; (5) Template-based QA generation for robotic-centric perception tasks using metadata.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Preprocessing follows dimension-specific pipelines: (1) Instruction: explicit instructions from daily-life scenarios are rewritten into implicit forms using LLMs; (2) Perception: robotic data with type/view metadata for template-based QA, Gemini-segmented video steps for temporal grounding, human-labeled bounding boxes for task-centric perception; (3) Planning: frame sequences extracted from videos, Gemini generates structured annotations (task summaries, step-wise instructions with timestamps, metadata), refined by human annotators, steps mapped into function templates; (4) Affordance: representative frames sampled with three annotation types (static contact points, dynamic motion trajectories, mobile base positions); (5) Failure: execution failures from RoboMIND labeled by experts, planning failures synthesized by perturbation. Quality control includes two-stage filtering: general criteria (image quality, task validity) and task-specific rules, followed by validation by 20 professionally trained annotators and majority-vote strategy for item removal/correction.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations are created through multiple methods: (1) MLLM-based annotation: Gemini generates structured annotations including task summaries, step-wise instructions with timestamps, metadata (objects, actions, scenes, embodiments), video segmentation for temporal grounding, and functional object properties; (2) Human expert annotation: 20 professionally trained annotators validate linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness; experts label execution-level failures from RoboMIND; human annotators refine Gemini-generated annotations and provide bounding boxes for task-centric perception; (3) Template-based annotation: robotic-centric perception uses metadata for template-based QA generation; (4) Affordance annotation: three types annotated - static (contact points), dynamic (motion trajectories), and mobile (base positions). Each step in planning tasks is mapped into function templates grouped into manipulation or navigation skill lists.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Quality control adopts a two-stage process: (1) Construction stage filtering with general criteria (image quality, task validity) and task-specific rules (e.g., excluding single-arm data from dual-arm tasks); (2) Post-construction validation by 20 professionally trained annotators checking linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness; (3) Majority-vote strategy: items all models solve correctly are removed, items all models fail undergo manual review and correction. For planning evaluation, an MLLM-as-world-simulator framework assesses both structural correctness and embodied feasibility by simulating whether plans achieve critical object-state milestones.
rai:annotationsPerItem: Variable by dimension. Planning tasks include three evaluation types (Q1: long-horizon planning, Q2: next-step planning, Q3: task state estimation). Perception and failure analysis use multiple-choice format. Affordance prediction includes point prediction and trajectory prediction. Human annotations refined MLLM-generated structured annotations for planning tasks.
rai:annotatorDemographics: 20 professionally trained annotators were recruited for quality inspection and validation. No additional demographic information is provided.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini (Comanici et al. 2025) for video segmentation, structured annotation generation (task summaries, step-wise instructions, metadata extraction), temporal grounding, and functional property generation. GPT for generating functional object properties and distractors, and for explicit-to-implicit instruction conversion.
rai:dataSocialImpact: RoboBench aims to advance robotic intelligence by providing a comprehensive evaluation framework for MLLMs as embodied brains. The benchmark enables systematic assessment of cognitive capabilities required for manipulation tasks, helping identify limitations in current models and guide development of more robust embodied AI systems. By establishing evaluation standards across instruction comprehension, perception, planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis, RoboBench contributes to building safer and more capable robotic systems for real-world deployment.
rai:dataBiases: The benchmark acknowledges potential biases: (1) Dataset sources primarily from existing robotic manipulation datasets which may reflect biases in task selection, object types, and environmental settings; (2) Planning evaluation relies on MLLM-as-world-simulator which may introduce model-specific biases in assessment; (3) Human annotation by 20 trained annotators may reflect annotator-specific interpretation biases; (4) Implicit instruction generation using LLMs may introduce language model biases in task formulation; (5) The benchmark focuses on manipulation tasks which may not generalize to other embodied AI domains.
rai:dataLimitations: Known limitations include: (1) Execution-level failure diagnosis remains intrinsically difficult, with even human evaluators achieving only 47.30 compared to 80.67 on planning errors; (2) Current models show severe degradation on implicit instructions (average 30% score drop); (3) Models struggle with dual-arm coordination and rare-object reasoning; (4) Multi-view inputs provide modest gains but do not close the gap to human performance; (5) The benchmark reveals that current MLLMs exhibit only superficial embodied reasoning and world-modeling capabilities; (6) Planning evaluation framework, while more faithful than text similarity metrics, still relies on MLLM simulation which has inherent limitations; (7) Dataset construction relies partially on synthetic data generation (e.g., planning failures, implicit instructions) which may not fully capture real-world complexity.
rai:dataUseCases: RoboBench is designed for: (1) Evaluating MLLMs as embodied brains across five cognitive dimensions (instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, failure analysis); (2) Benchmarking state-of-the-art MLLMs to identify bottlenecks in embodied cognition; (3) Guiding development of next-generation MLLMs toward more robust robotic intelligence; (4) Assessing generalization across embodiments (single-arm, dual-arm, mobile manipulator, humanoid), objects (material attributes, physical properties, world knowledge), views (multi-view integration under occlusion), and tasks (navigation with spatial cues); (5) Testing both closed-source and open-source MLLMs including embodied-specific models. The benchmark provides a leaderboard and actionable insights for advancing embodied AI research. Not recommended for: deployment decisions without additional real-world validation, as the benchmark focuses on cognitive evaluation rather than end-to-end task execution success.
